rule.description: A group of two or more consecutive named parameters, matched by name and type, that appears as the same run in at least three distinct method signatures of package golang.zx2c4.com/wireguard/device instead of being held by one cohesive data type. Receiverless package functions and test files are outside the rule; within one signature only the locally longest qualifying run is credited.

checks.description: The UAPI set operation's peer-selection state is threaded as bare consecutive pointer parameters through sibling configuration stages.
checks.detected_relation: per-operation UAPI configuration state -> sibling per-line and post-configuration stage method signatures
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The peer pointer being operated on, its placeholder/dummy provenance, and its created-during-this-operation flag are produced by one set operation, share one lifetime, and take meaning only from each other; threading them as three separate in-out parameters forces every stage to restate the grouping and blocks giving the state behavior of its own.

matches.evidence: signature (device *Device) handlePostConfig(peer **Peer, dummy *bool, created *bool, pkaOn *bool) receives the recurring run (peer **Peer, dummy *bool, created *bool) before its keepalive trailing parameter
signature (device *Device) handlePublicKeyLine(peer **Peer, dummy *bool, created *bool, value string) threads the same run plus the parsed public key line
signature (device *Device) handlePeerLine(peer **Peer, dummy *bool, created *bool, pkaOn *bool, key, value string) threads the same run plus its keepalive flag and the configuration key/value pair

checks.description: The inbound handshake datagram context (verbatim packet bytes and remote endpoint) is threaded as bare consecutive parameters through every stage that validates, dispatches, consumes, or answers it.
checks.detected_relation: one received handshake datagram (payload, remote endpoint) -> sibling validation, dispatch, consumption, and denial-reply method signatures
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The payload and the source address describe a single datagram produced by one receive; validation needs both, dispatch needs both, consumption needs both, and the denial reply needs the endpoint to answer; carrying them as two separate parameters through six sibling signatures restates one record in every signature.

matches.evidence: signature (device *Device) handleHandshakeMsg(msgType uint32, packet []byte, endpoint conn.Endpoint) carries the recurring run (packet []byte, endpoint conn.Endpoint) after its dispatch parameter
signature (device *Device) processCookieReply(packet []byte, endpoint conn.Endpoint) decodes the reply from the payload and attributes it to the datagram source

signature (device *Device) authenticateHandshake(packet []byte, endpoint conn.Endpoint) bool validates MACs against the payload, consults the source address, and forwards both members when a cookie is owed

signature (device *Device) processHandshakeInitiation(packet []byte, endpoint conn.Endpoint) decodes the initiation, learns the endpoint from the datagram source, and accounts bytes for the payload length
signature (device *Device) processHandshakeResponse(packet []byte, endpoint conn.Endpoint) decodes the response, learns the endpoint, and derives the session from the same pair
signature (device *Device) SendHandshakeCookie(packet []byte, endpoint conn.Endpoint) error builds the denial reply from the denied payload and answers toward the datagram source it was handed

checks.description: The Noise transcript working state (mix hash and chain key) is threaded alongside per-stage message and handshake views through every staging method of the handshake consumption.
checks.detected_relation: borrowed transcript working memory with adjacent stage context -> sibling transcript staging method signatures
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The hash and chain-key arrays are one borrowed transcript that every stage must observe through the same backings for the protocol transcript to stay sound; restating both arrays (plus the adjacent handshake or message view) in four sibling signatures leaves the transcript's ownership entirely implicit in the parameter order.

matches.evidence: signature (device *Device) mixInitiationTranscript(msg *MessageInitiation, hash *[blake2s.Size]byte, chainKey *[blake2s.Size]byte) threads the locally longest recurring run (msg *MessageInitiation, hash, chainKey)

signature (device *Device) decryptInitiationStatic(msg *MessageInitiation, hash *[blake2s.Size]byte, chainKey *[blake2s.Size]byte) (peerPK NoisePublicKey, ok bool) threads the same three-member run while deriving the peer static

signature (device *Device) verifyInitiationTimestamp(handshake *Handshake, msg *MessageInitiation, hash *[blake2s.Size]byte, chainKey *[blake2s.Size]byte) (timestamp tai64n.Timestamp, replay bool, flood bool, ok bool) carries the same run behind its handshake view

signature (device *Device) consumeResponseTranscript(handshake *Handshake, msg *MessageResponse, hash *[blake2s.Size]byte, chainKey *[blake2s.Size]byte) bool threads the (hash, chainKey) working-memory run, which recurs across all four staging signatures

excluded.target: device/noise-helpers.go KDF1/KDF2/KDF3 and HMAC1/HMAC2 (recurring key/input parameter tuples)
excluded.reason: receiverless arity-variant helper families that deliberately expose parallel whole-signature tuples; whole-signature uniformity is a designed API family, not partially-encapsulated state, so receiverless functions are out of the rule's scope

excluded.target: conn package receive-function constructors and bind plumbing
excluded.reason: outside the analyzed device package; those signatures are dictated by the conn.ReceiveFunc interface and by batching plumbing

excluded.target: test files, unnamed parameters, and blank parameters
excluded.reason: parameters without names cannot establish a named grouping, and test code is out of scope for the production smell relation
